system: You are an autonomous research agent working for a physics collaboration. You have tools for simulations, queries and project documents. Work through the task on your own; you cannot ask anyone questions. When you are done, call submit_recommendation exactly once.
user:
Task brief:
{
  "task_description": "Design the Level-1 trigger algorithm for a new signature at an LHC experiment. Use the simulation and the project documents to choose the algorithm and its threshold.",
  "goal": "Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.",
  "constraints": [
    "The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.",
    "The algorithm must be deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware.",
    "Threshold between 20 and 60 GeV.",
    "Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold."
  ]
}

result:
# Candidate algorithms
- Algorithm-L1: iterative topological clustering with a learned calibration.
- Algorithm-L3: sliding-window clustering with a learned calibration.
- Algorithm-L2: fixed-window sum.
All fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs).

# Rate allocation
The new signature is allocated 8 kHz of the Level-1 bandwidth.

# Earlier emulation summary (2025, 35 GeV threshold)
Signal efficiency at the allocated rate: Algorithm-L1 92%, Algorithm-L3 85%, Algorithm-L2 74%.

# Meeting notes 2026-06-03
The trigger menu review is in September. Monitoring histograms are defined.

content.text:
Good! Now I understand the context:
- Three candidate algorithms (Algorithm-L1, Algorithm-L2, Algorithm-L3)
- All fit within FPGA resource budget
- Allocated rate: 8 kHz
- Previous simulation at 35 GeV showed Algorithm-L1 had the best efficiency (92%), followed by Algorithm-L3 (85%) and Algorithm-L2 (74%)

Now let me run simulations to find the optimal threshold for each algorithm. I'll test different thresholds within the 20-60 GeV range to determine which combination gives the highest signal efficiency at the allocated 8 kHz rate.

Let me start by testing each algorithm at different threshold values:

Good! This confirms the 2025 simulation results. Algorithm-L1 is clearly the best at 35 GeV. Now let me explore different thresholds to see if I can improve the efficiency further. Let me test lower thresholds first:

Interesting! At 30 GeV, Algorithm-L1 achieves slightly higher efficiency (92.492%) than at 35 GeV (92.162%). However, lower thresholds (25 and 20 GeV) show decreased efficiency. Let me test a few more values around 30-35 GeV to find the optimal point:
The efficiency peaks around 30 GeV (92.492%) for Algorithm-L1. Let me verify by testing a couple more points around 30:
Perfect! The data shows that 30 GeV gives the best efficiency for Algorithm-L1 (92.492%). Let me also check if the other algorithms might achieve better performance at different thresholds:
Even at 30 GeV, Algorithm-L3 (85.673%) and Algorithm-L2 (73.244%) significantly underperform Algorithm-L1 (92.492%). Let me verify that higher thresholds don't improve L3 or L2:

The results are clear. Algorithm-L1 at 30 GeV threshold provides the best signal efficiency (92.492%) at the allocated 8 kHz rate. This is significantly better than the other algorithms at any tested threshold.

Let me now submit my recommendation:

input.justification:
Based on comprehensive simulation testing, Algorithm-L1 with a 30 GeV threshold achieves the highest signal efficiency of 92.492% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. This represents the optimal configuration among all tested combinations:

- Algorithm-L1 at 30 GeV: 92.492% efficiency (RECOMMENDED)
- Algorithm-L1 at 35 GeV: 92.162% efficiency  
- Algorithm-L3 at 30 GeV: 85.673% efficiency
- Algorithm-L2 at 35 GeV: 74.279% efficiency

The iterative topological clustering with learned calibration (Algorithm-L1) outperforms both the sliding-window clustering (Algorithm-L3) and fixed-window sum (Algorithm-L2) approaches. The 30 GeV threshold represents the optimal operating point, providing ~0.3% higher efficiency than the previously studied 35 GeV threshold while maintaining the allocated rate. Lower thresholds (25, 28 GeV) showed decreased efficiency, indicating 30 GeV is near the optimal balance.
